method: Every expected_outcome is the application's real behaviour, established by probing Juice Shop directly with curl and a plain browser before AuthFlowGuard was run. The ground_truth field records that probe. A case passes only when AuthFlowGuard reports what the application actually does. The quiet profile changes presentation only (welcome banner, challenge notifications, hints, tutorial); the probes were repeated under it and gave identical results.

cases.ground_truth: POST /rest/user/login returns HTTP 401 with the identical body 'Invalid email or password.' for a known email with a wrong password and for an unknown email.
cases.rationale: Failed-login responses are indistinguishable, so login does not reveal whether an account exists.

cases.ground_truth: POST /api/Users with an existing email returns HTTP 400 'email must be unique'; with a fresh email it returns HTTP 201 and creates the account.
cases.rationale: Registration discloses that an email is already registered.
cases.notes: The identifier contains {run}, so each run registers a new account and the case stays repeatable against a long-lived container.

cases.ground_truth: GET /rest/user/security-question returns the account's security question for a known email and an empty object for an unknown email.
cases.rationale: The password-reset flow discloses whether an email belongs to an account.

cases.ground_truth: Six consecutive wrong-password attempts for the admin account each returned HTTP 401, and the correct password immediately afterwards returned HTTP 200.
cases.rationale: No lockout or throttling restricts the valid control after repeated failures.
cases.notes: Juice Shop never locks the account, so this case cannot disturb the others.

cases.ground_truth: No token cookie exists before login; the only pre-login cookies are language and banner preferences. Login mints a new JWT, so there is no pre-login session identifier to fix.
cases.rationale: Replaying the pre-login cookie state cannot reach the account.

cases.ground_truth: Logging out sends no request to the server. Replaying the pre-logout token cookie in a fresh browser context still renders /profile with the account's email.
cases.rationale: Logout clears the token only in the browser; the server continues to accept it.
cases.notes: Juice Shop's logout is a client-side menu button, not an HTML form that submits a POST.
